question: What will the first reported revenues after September 2026 be for the following companies? (Microsoft)

calls.reasoning: Guidance for FQ1 FY27 is $89.85-90.95B. Over the last 8 quarters Microsoft beat the top of guidance by $0.5-2.2B (median ~$1.0B; Q1s ~$0.6-1.0B; most recent FQ4 FY26 +$2.2B: $90.0B vs $87.8B top). Last year revenue rose ~1.6% from Q4 to Q1, so a flat-sequential guide looks conservative, though FQ4 may have held one-off items. Azure guided ~45% cc. Consensus is ~$90.6-90.7B (one outlier at $92.45B). Median ~$91.95B. No Kalshi, Polymarket or Manifold market found.
calls.dossier:
- Resolves off Microsoft's FQ1 FY2027 (Jul-Sep 2026) total revenue in its initial earnings release (8-K), expected Oct 28, 2026, after market close. Later revisions don't count.
- Event window: quarter ended Sep 30, 2026; release expected Oct 28, 2026. As of Oct 23, 2026 the quarter is 100% elapsed and the result is unpublished.
- Guidance (Amy Hood, Jul 29, 2026 FQ4 call): revenue $89.85-90.95B (+16-17% YoY). Agents & Infra $75.15-75.75B, Devices & Consumer $14.7-15.2B (new 2-segment reporting from FY27). Another source gives an old-segment split: Intelligent Cloud $40.95-41.25B, PBP $36.7-37.0B. Azure ~45% cc (StreetAccount consensus was 41.4% at the time). Capex ~$50B.
- FQ4 FY26 actual: $90.007B vs guidance top $87.8B (beat top by $2.2B) and consensus $87.63B. Azure grew 43% cc vs 39.5% guided (Yahoo/Morningstar, Jul 2026).
- Revenue over the prior 8 quarters ($M): 65,585; 69,632; 70,066; 76,441; 77,673; 81,273; 82,886; 90,007.
- Beat vs top of guidance, approx., from memory (FY25 Q1 -> FY26 Q4): +0.6, +0.5, +1.4, +2.2, +1.0, +0.7, +1.1, +2.2 ($B). Q1 beats were the smaller ones.
- Q4->Q1 change: FY25Q4 76.44 -> FY26Q1 77.67 (+1.6%). The FY27Q1 guide midpoint is about flat vs FY26Q4 90.0, so either the guide is conservative or FQ4 had one-off strength (EPS one-offs: $3.2B Anthropic gain, a non-revenue item).
- Consensus: MarketBeat $90.62B, Visible Alpha ~$90.7B, one other source $92.453B (Oct 2026).
- Stock up ~39% since Jun 30. Previews say the report needs revenue above $90.95B.
- FX: searched; found no explicit FX assumption or dollar move data for the quarter.
- Markets: no Polymarket, Manifold or Kalshi contract found.

calls.reasoning: Microsoft guided Q1 FY27 revenue to $89.85-90.95B (midpoint ~$90.4B); sell-side consensus is ~$90.6-90.7B. Over the last 8 quarters, actual revenue beat the guidance midpoint by +0.9% to +3.7% (mean ~2.35%): Q4 FY26 came in at $90.0B against a $86.7-87.8B guide, and Q1 FY26 at $77.7B against $74.7-75.8B. FX was roughly neutral over Jul-Sep 2026: the dollar was soft in Jul-Aug and rallied in September, and EUR/USD finished the quarter about flat. Management expects Windows OEM revenue to fall by a high-teens percentage, and some of Q4's large beat may not repeat, so I trimmed the beat slightly: median ~$92.2B. The chance of landing below $90.2B (a miss of the guidance low end) or above $94.5B is each well under 3%, so I declare no escape mass. No Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market was found.
calls.dossier:
- Microsoft Q1 FY27 (quarter ending Sep 30, 2026) results are scheduled for Oct 28, 2026, after the market close (MarketBeat, Benzinga, Oct 2026).
- Company guidance given in the late-July 2026 Q4 call: total revenue $89.85-90.95B, up 16-17% YoY; the year-ago quarter was $77.673B. Azure guided to ~45% constant-currency growth. Capex guided above $50B. Windows OEM & Devices expected to decline by a high-teens percentage in FY27. This is the first report under a new two-segment structure (TIKR; Benzinga; Oct 2026).
- Sell-side consensus is roughly $90.58-90.71B, depending on the aggregator (Zacks, Visible Alpha, MarketBeat; Oct 2026). TIKR notes consensus sits near the top of the guidance range.
- Beat history, actual vs guidance midpoint: Q1 FY25 65.59 vs 65.0 (+0.9%); Q2 FY25 69.63 vs 68.6 (+1.5%); Q3 FY25 70.07 vs 68.2 (+2.7%); Q4 FY25 76.44 vs 73.7 (+3.7%); Q1 FY26 77.67 vs 75.25 (+3.2%); Q2 FY26 81.27 vs 80.05 (+1.5%); Q3 FY26 82.89 vs 81.2 (+2.1%); Q4 FY26 90.01 vs 87.25 (+3.2%; guide was $86.7-87.8B per CNBC Apr 29, 2026). Guidance ranges for earlier quarters are from memory; Q4 FY26 is confirmed by search. In no quarter did revenue land below the guidance midpoint. Mean beat ~2.35%, SD ~0.95%.
- Q4 FY26 revenue of $90.01B beat consensus of $87.62B (Benzinga).
- FX: the DXY softened in Jul-Aug 2026, then rose about 2.4% Sep 9-25 after a Fed hike. EUR/USD monthly averages were 1.1423 (Jul), 1.1594 (Aug), 1.1505 (Sep) (Fed G.5; MTFX). Net effect vs late-July guidance rates is roughly neutral.
- Resolves off the total revenue figure in Microsoft's Q1 FY27 8-K/press release as initially reported; later revisions do not count.

calls.reasoning: Microsoft guided Q1 FY27 revenue to $89.85–90.95B (midpoint $90.4B). Consensus is about $90.6–90.7B. Over FY26 the company beat its guidance midpoint by roughly 1.5–3.2% every quarter. Q4 FY26 came in at $90.0B, 2.7% above LSEG consensus, because GPU capacity arrived faster than planned. Applying that beat rate gives a median near $92.4B. Downside risks are capacity timing and FX (guidance assumed a drag of under 1 point). Upside comes from Azure growing faster than the guided 45%. Market check: Polymarket has a 'beat estimates' market at about 95% and an Azure/cloud revenue threshold market (>$61.5B at 86%). Neither contract matches total revenue, so I treated both as weak evidence, not as anchors. I found no Kalshi total-revenue market.

calls.reasoning: Guide $89.85-90.95B (mid $90.4B), consensus ~$90.65B. Over the last 8 quarters MSFT beat the guidance midpoint by 0.9-3.7% (mean ~2.35%) and never missed it; the last 4 quarters averaged ~2.5%, or ~$1.5B above the guidance top. FX was roughly neutral over Jul-Sep 2026. I trimmed slightly for possible one-off strength in Q4 FY26 and the Windows OEM decline. Median ~$92.3B. No matching Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold total-revenue market was found; Polymarket 'beat estimates' (~95%) and Azure contracts are near-miss evidence only.
calls.reconciliation: The runs agreed on guidance ($89.85-90.95B), consensus (~$90.6-90.7B), the FQ4 FY26 actual ($90.007B vs $86.7-87.8B guide) and the release date (Oct 28). The one factual dispute: Run 1 said Q1 beats run smaller (~$1.0B over the top), while Runs 2 and 3 put Q1 FY26 at $77.67B vs a $74.7-75.8B guide (~+$1.9B over the top, +3.2% over the midpoint). Runs 2 and 3 are consistent with each other and with my memory of the guide, so I set Run 1's seasonal discount aside. The remaining differences were judgment: how much of the recent ~2.5% midpoint beat persists. I take a median slightly under the beat-implied ~$92.5-92.7B because of the Windows OEM decline, capacity limits and possible Q4 one-offs. I carried forward Run 2's ~$2.2B dispersion. I could not re-verify FX on this run (no web access), so I relied on Run 2's G.5 data, which shows it roughly neutral.

disagreements.claim: Q1 beats are seasonally smaller (FY26 Q1 ~ +$1.0B over the guide top)
disagreements.verdict: Likely wrong: Runs 2 and 3 give a $74.7-75.8B guide vs $77.67B actual (~+$1.9B over the top), which matches my memory
